title: Can a household add-on be created without an active primary membership?
content:
## Product and scope
This document states the Household Add-On Membership basis for what the primary member's own club membership must show before a household add-on may be created for them, and how the add-on's discounts relate to that membership.

## Rule
A household add-on may be created only for a primary member who already holds an active club membership. The add-on's own discounts, including guest-pass sharing, class-booking inclusion, and the personal-training and locker-rental discount rates, are bundled onto that same club membership, and the add-on cannot exist independently of it.

## Eligibility: what must be true before an add-on may be created
- Applicable event: the creation of a new household add-on for a primary member.
- Authority: the primary member's club membership status is read from the system's own record of that membership, not from anything the customer states on the call.
- Object correlation: the membership status checked is the status of the club membership held by the same customer for whom the add-on is being created.
- Allowed status: active. A household add-on may not be created for a primary member whose club membership record shows any other status.

## Points of judgement
- The gate looks at the primary member's own club membership record, not at the dependent being added; the dependent has no membership record of its own to check.
- Because the add-on's discounts are bundled onto the primary member's club membership rather than issued independently, the add-on has no free-standing existence: it is created only in relation to, and remains dependent on, that specific active club membership.
